de32_ice.topic: ICE as the template: origin, money, hiring and training, reassigned agents, city surges, killings, deaths in custody, citizens detained, masks and ID

claims.text: ICE opened on 1 March 2003 as a component of DHS, created by the Homeland Security Act signed 25 November 2002 'in response to 9/11'; it took the enforcement functions of the INS and the Customs Service and holds 'a unique combination of civil and criminal authorities'

H.R. 1 (signed 4 July 2025): $45bn for detention, $29.9bn lump sum for ICE enforcement and removal incl. hiring, 10,000 new ICE officers over five years, $13.5bn state reimbursement, $1bn DoD; funds to 30 Sep 2029; $170.7bn immigration/border total
DHS (5 Jan 2026): ICE hired more than 12,000 officers and agents, workforce from about 10,000 to 22,000; McLaughlin: 'a 120% increase'; more than 220,000 applications (the agency's own figures)

ICE's FAQ: almost five months of training (five weeks language, 16 weeks law enforcement); DHS official (8 Jan 2026): 'Training ... is 8 weeks long'; Atlantic's '47 days' from unnamed officials, DHS called it 'false'; PolitiFact rated 'Mostly True'

29 deaths in ICE custody in FY2026 by mid-April 2026, passing FY2004's 28; Ossoff-Warnock letter (13 Apr 2026): 49 since Jan 2025; El Paso medical examiner ruled Geraldo Lunas Campos's death at Camp East Montana a homicide ('asphyxia due to neck and torso compression'); FBI investigating; DHS said death rate 0.009%

Judge Sara Ellis's 233-page opinion (Nov 2025): 'video disproves Defendants' contentions'; Bovino admitted lying about a rock before tear gas in Little Village; an agent used ChatGPT to write a use-of-force report; the 7th Circuit had called the injunction 'overbroad'

ICE officer Jonathan Ross shot Renee Good on 7 Jan 2026; Alex Pretti was shot 24 Jan 2026 (ProPublica named Border Patrol agent Jesus Ochoa and CBP officer Raymundo Gutierrez; DHS did not confirm); no federal investigation of Good; evidence handed to Hennepin County in July 2026 after a state suit; no charging decisions; ICE agent Christian Castro charged with four counts of second-degree assault and false report in the Sosa-Celis shooting

Judge Christina Snyder (10 Feb 2026) blocked California's mask ban as applied to federal agents because it exempted state police, and upheld the requirement to display agency and badge number: 'federal officers can perform their federal functions without wearing masks'

Cato (Bier): an ICE disclosure counted 42,153 personnel diverted to ERO, 5-28 Aug 2025, 28,390 from federal law enforcement; per-agency estimates FBI 2,840, DEA 2,181, ATF 1,778, USMS 650, HSI 6,198; up to 600 State Dept security agents deputised
IRS-CI deployed 250 agents to immigration work since May 2025 (chief Guy Ficco, AP)
ProPublica (Oct 2026): 506 US citizens detained by immigration agents, at least 70 minors, 36 held a day or more without lawyer or family contact, about a dozen deported, mostly children

Noem v. Vasquez Perdomo (8 Sep 2025, 6-3) stayed a restraining order barring stops based on apparent race or ethnicity, accent, location or type of work; Kavanaugh: factors 'constitute at least reasonable suspicion'; Sotomayor: people who 'look a certain way' targeted

claims.text: ICE's page (data as of 15 Feb 2025): 137 287(g) agreements, 60 jail enforcement, 75 warrant service officer, 2 task force; 287(g) of the INA added by IIRIRA 1996

Kocher's tally of ICE spreadsheets: 135 agreements in Jan 2025, 444 in April, 896 across about 690 agencies on 15 Aug 2025; 443 task-force; Florida 318, Texas 137; none in CA, CT, DE, HI, IL, NJ, OR, WA

FWD.us: 1,372 agreements across 1,169 agencies as of 26 Jan 2026, 764 task-force; ICE reported 8,501 local officers trained under TFM by Sep 2025; since Sep 2025 ICE pays salary, benefits, start-up costs, overtime and arrest-linked 'performance' bonuses; FWD.us estimates $1.4-2bn in 2026; Obama administration ended TFM at end of 2012 after abuses incl. Maricopa County; Dallas declined a reported $25M offer
Texas SB 8 (effective 1 Jan 2026): sheriffs who run jails must enter a 287(g) agreement by December 2026; the attorney general can sue refusers; grants for counties under 1 million

Judge Ramon Reyes (E.D.N.Y., Oct 2026) dismissed the DOJ suit against NYC's sanctuary laws: federal law does not require local information-sharing and the federal government cannot force local governments to help enforce immigration law
Printz v. United States (1997, 5-4) struck the Brady Act's command to sheriffs; Scalia: 'Such commands are fundamentally incompatible with our constitutional system of dual sovereignty'

In 2018 DHS contractor LookingGlass compiled more than 600 planned 'Family Separation Day' protests and disseminated it to fusion centres; DHS called the list 'unsolicited' (FOIA emails via The Intercept)

de32_military.topic: The military at home: Posse Comitatus, Insurrection Act threats, Guard deployments and rulings (LA, Portland, Illinois, DC), QRFs, NDAs, firings, Quantico, Department of War title, bases as detention, precedents

claims.text: 18 U.S.C. 1385: whoever wilfully uses any part of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force or Space Force as a posse comitatus or otherwise to execute the laws, except where the Constitution or an Act of Congress expressly authorises, faces fine or up to two years; source act 18 June 1878
Breyer entered partial judgment for California on its Posse Comitatus Act claims after a bench trial on 2 Sep 2025 (Dkt. 186)

About 4,000 Guard federalised and 700 Marines in LA (June 2025); Breyer warned of 'creating a national police force with the President as its chief' and barred uses such as riot control, arrests and traffic stops in California

Trump v. Illinois (23 Dec 2025): stay application denied 6-3; 'regular forces' likely means the military; the government 'failed to identify a source of authority' to let the military execute the laws in Illinois; Kavanaugh concurred; Alito: 'wary of using soldiers as domestic police'; interim posture
Judge Karin Immergut permanently barred the Portland Guard deployment: 'The President's determination was simply untethered to the facts'; no rebellion or danger of one

Judge Jia Cobb (20 Nov 2025) ruled the DC deployment for crime control and out-of-state troops unlawful; D.C. Circuit (Katsas, Millett, Rao) stayed it 17 Dec 2025, citing 'a unique power within the District'; 2,200+ Guard; Spc. Sarah Beckstrom killed, SSgt Andrew Wolfe wounded, 26 Nov 2025

Trump on Truth Social, 15 Jan 2026: 'I will institute the INSURRECTION ACT' if Minnesota politicians did not stop 'professional agitators and insurrectionists'; Act of 1807; last invoked 1992 Los Angeles; Brennan Center counts 30 uses; prior threat over Portland
About 1,500 soldiers of the 11th Airborne put on prepare-to-deploy orders (disclosed 18 Jan 2026) to go only if the Act was invoked; Trump: no reason 'right now', 'If I needed it, I'd use it'
Quantico, 30 Sep 2025: 'We should use some of these dangerous cities as training grounds for our military'; 'We're under invasion from within'; Hegseth: 'do the honorable thing and resign'
Quantico: 'It's a war from within'; 'straighten them out, one-by-one'

21 Feb 2025: Gen. CQ Brown, Adm. Lisa Franchetti, Gen. James Slife and Army JAG Lt. Gen. Joseph Berger III and Air Force JAG Lt. Gen. Charles Plummer removed; Navy JAG had retired; Hegseth: JAGs not 'well-suited'

National Guard Bureau memos (Oct 2025, Maj. Gen. Ronald Burkett): quick reaction forces in each state, often 500, over 23,000 total; quarter deployable in 8 hours, all in a day; operational by 1 Jan 2026; crowd-control, batons, shields, Tasers, pepper spray; citing an August executive order

New Mexico National Defense Area unveiled 18 April 2025 (~180 miles); Magistrate Judge Gregory Wormuth dismissed trespass counts: complaint failed to show the defendant 'knew he/she was entering' the zone; up to 400 cases

Camp East Montana at Fort Bliss: up to 5,000, soft-sided structures, up to 72 per pod; HRW/ACLU report 15 Jul 2026 from 80 interviews (Oct 2025-Jun 2026) alleging beatings and medical neglect; internal ICE investigation documented unreported uses of force

Guantánamo: memo 29 Jan 2025; first transfer 4 Feb 2025; peak 178; ~$40M first month; ~1,100 troops; 832 transferred in year to May 2026; ~400 beds, <2% occupied (CBS 14 May 2026); Escalona v. Noem filed 1 Mar 2025
EO 14347 (5 Sep 2025) authorises 'Department of War' and 'Secretary of War' as secondary titles; statutory references unchanged until Congress acts; directs legislative proposals
EO 10730 (23/24 Sep 1957) federalised the Arkansas Guard and sent 1,000 101st Airborne paratroopers to enforce desegregation of Central High against Gov. Faubus's use of the Guard
Defense Secretary Esper, 3 Jun 2020: 'I do not support invoking the Insurrection Act'; 'We are not in one of those situations now'

About 1,700 Guard members authorised in 20 Republican-led states to assist ICE under Title 32 (clerical, transport, processing); Vermont Gov. Phil Scott refused; Nunn: Title 32 needs 'a cooperative governor'

de32_detention.topic: The detention business: private share, GEO and CoreCivic contracts, revenue, stock, political money, EO 14006/14148, bed guarantees, BI/ISAP monitoring, $1-a-day labour suits, Alligator Alcatraz, inspections

claims.text: About 90% of people ICE detained in early 2025 were in facilities owned or operated by private contractors

GEO FY2025: revenue $2,631.5M; net income $254.3M including a $232.4M pre-tax gain from selling Lawton CF to Oklahoma for $312M; adjusted EBITDA $464.4M; about 6,000 ICE beds added (about 20,000 to 26,000): Delaney Hall 1,000, North Lake 1,800, D. Ray James 1,868, North Florida 1,310, Adelanto 1,940; up to ~$520M annualised new revenue; 'the most successful year for new business wins in our Company's history'; two-year ICE skip-tracing contract Dec 2025; $90.6M buybacks; BI's new two-year ISAP contract 30 Sep 2025; $38.2M litigation reserve mainly Nwauzor

CoreCivic FY2025: revenue $2,211.2M (+13%), net income $116.5M (+69%); Q4 ICE revenue $244.7M vs $120.3M; 11.2M shares bought back for $218.4M; facilities Dilley (2,400), Farmville (acquired 1 Jul 2025), California City (2,560), West Tennessee (600), Diamondback (2,160); Midwest Regional pending a Special Use Permit

CoreCivic 10-K: ICE revenue $770.7M in 2025 (35%) vs $564.8M in 2024 (29%), 30% in 2023; 'we do not, under longstanding policy, lobby for or against policies or legislation' determining the basis or duration of detention; contracts 'guarantee the federal partner access to a minimum bed capacity in exchange for a fixed monthly payment'; 16 facilities with ICE as primary customer

GEO Q2 2026: revenue $732.1M (+15%), net income $47.5M, adjusted EBITDA $142.0M (+20%); Big Horn, Hudson CO, 1,188 beds, ~$85M/yr from 9 Jul 2026; Rivers, Winton NC, 1,320 beds, ~$80M/yr from 1 Aug 2026; ICE reimburses capex and start-up; FY2026 revenue guidance $2.95-3.05bn
Delaney Hall, Newark: 15-year fixed-price ICE contract, 1,000 beds, over $60M annualised revenue, about $1bn over the term (27 Feb 2025)
On 6 Nov 2024 CoreCivic stock rose 29% and GEO 42% in a single session
CoreCivic gave $500,000 to the Trump-Vance Inaugural Committee on 19 Dec 2024 (LDA report); CEO Hininger gave $300,000 to Trump's JFC; GEO Acquisitions II gave $1M to MAGA Inc. in 2024

GEO also gave $500,000 to the inaugural committee; GEO closed at $15.13 on Election Day; Zoley: 'an expected sea change', 'The GEO Group was built for this unique moment'; Bondi had been a registered lobbyist for GEO at Ballard Partners

2026 cycle: GEO Reentry Services LLC gave $4.4M to MAGA Inc. and $1.3M to the Congressional Leadership Fund; GEO PAC giving to party committees triple 2024; both PACs gave $10,000 to Rep. Garbarino; support 'overwhelmingly' Republican; CoreCivic said it educates policymakers
EO 14006 (26 Jan 2021) directed DOJ not to renew private prison contracts (BOP, USMS); it did not cover ICE/DHS; revoked 20 Jan 2025; ICE was 43% of GEO's and 30% of CoreCivic's revenue in 2023
GAO (Feb 2021): guaranteed-minimum contracts rose from 29 (FY2017) to 43 (FY2019); guaranteed beds 19,342 to 28,043; as of 11 May 2020 ICE paid for 12,027 empty beds a day, $20.5M for the month

GEO earnings call 6 Aug 2026: about 184,000 ISAP participants; nearly 54,000 on GPS ankle monitors, up from about 17,000 a year earlier; monitors earn more than $2 a day vs about $0.96 for SmartLINK; $16M invested in monitor production

CyberScoop (FOIA): 177,654 in SmartLINK in FY2023; ICE contract gives 'unlimited rights to use, dispose of, or disclose' ISAP data; BI collects facial images and voice prints; location data contributed to 40 arrests in Virginia (2018); PIA says seven-year retention, FOIA records suggest indefinite

A 1950 law funded payment for detainee work; Congress funded $1 a day; INS asked for $4 in 1982 and Congress did not act; PBNDS: 'at least $1 per day'; allegations of solitary for refusing work at Aurora, San Diego, Georgia

Nwauzor/Washington v. GEO: $17.3M back pay to more than 10,000 detainees (jury, 2021) and $5.9M unjust enrichment, $23.2M; $1 a day; 9th Circuit affirmed 16 Jan 2025: 'GEO is a private for-profit employer'
No. 25-828: petition 9 Jan 2026; CVSG 18 May 2026; US amicus brief filed 15 Sep 2026; supplemental briefs 29 Sep; distributed for conference of 6 Nov 2026; no decision as of 28 Oct 2026

Respondents' supplemental brief says the Solicitor General argues 'certiorari is necessary', that Washington's laws discriminate against federal contractors, and that the ruling 'threatens to upend' ICE's reliance on private contractors

GEO v. Menocal (25 Feb 2026): Kagan for the Court; Yearsley is a merits defence, not immunity; denial not immediately appealable; underlying claims: unpaid sanitation policy with sanctions up to 72 hours solitary (federal forced-labour bar) and $1-a-day work (unjust enrichment)

Alligator Alcatraz opened 1 Jul 2025, run by Florida DEM; $72.7M to 12 emergency vendors (24 Jun-7 Jul); $390.2M through October 2025; projected ~$1.065bn to 30 Jun 2026; FEMA $608.4M approved 30 Sep 2025 with conditions, revised 15 Dec to bar modification costs; Deportation Depot opened 5 Sep 2025

DHS OIG (OIG-26-22, Sep 2026; unannounced Jan 2026 inspection): less than half required living space; ~18 sq ft cages for up to two hours, once as punishment; legal phones not working; staff unsure which standards applied; ICE said Florida ran it under 287(g)
11th Circuit (21 Apr 2026, Pryor; Abudu dissenting) vacated the August 2025 wind-down injunction: 'Until Homeland Security officials decide to fund the facility, no final agency action occurs'

POGO (Aug 2026): four deaths at GEO's Adelanto since Aug 2025, most of any facility; 'superior' inspection grades tripled since 2024 and deficiencies fell 68% (2022-25) with weakened standards and fewer inspections; ICE did not respond

de32_stops.topic: What stops it: courts, governors, refusals and their limits, the Kelly ruling, polling-place statutes, the end of surges

claims.text: Judge Richard Leon granted Sen. Mark Kelly a preliminary injunction blocking the Pentagon's discipline (Feb 2026): Hegseth 'trampled on Senator Kelly's First Amendment freedoms'; six lawmakers' November video told service members they can refuse illegal orders; Trump called it seditious and punishable by death; a grand jury reportedly declined to indict; Hegseth said he would appeal

Orders are presumed lawful except 'manifestly illegal' ones judged by a person 'of ordinary sense and understanding'; a debatable order must be obeyed; an order 'is disobeyed at the peril of the subordinate' (MCM); no documented 2025-26 domestic refusal in the explainer
Col. Doug Krugman (USMC, 24 years) resigned in late Sep 2025; wrote service members 'should be confident in questioning possibly immoral or illegal orders'

18 U.S.C. 592 bars troops or armed men at polling places; 593 bars military interference with voters or election officers; Trump told the NYT (7 Jan 2026) he regretted not having the Guard seize voting machines in 2020; Wiles: troops at polls 'categorically false, will not happen'; Illinois order functionally limits Guard deployments to consenting states
Homan announced the 'imminent end' of Operation Metro Surge on 12 Feb 2026; about 3,000 agents at peak, DHS's largest; agents shot three people in a month, killing two; massive protests

7th Circuit (Brennan, Scudder; Easterbrook dissenting) vacated Ellis's injunction after plaintiffs' dismissal, calling it 'overbroad, constitutionally suspect'; Bovino's agents left Chicago soon after the 8 Nov injunction; Bovino reassigned in January after the Minneapolis killings
